## Standing Preferences (edit freely)

**Location:** Englewood, CO — King Soopers via Instacart

**Servings per dish:** 2
**Dinners per week:** 5 (eats out often — never assume 7)

**Notes from The Critic:**
- Eight weeks, **34 dish ratings; 29 of 34 at 4★+ (85%)**. Four "Cook again: No" verdicts (Cuban pork chops, Lomo Saltado, Greek meatball bowls) plus the single 1★ (Creamy Cajun Shrimp Pasta). Week 07-27 added **zero** to either list — the first fully clean week.
- **REHEAT QUALITY IS WORKING AS A CRITERION, AND WEEK 07-27 PROVES IT BOTH WAYS.** The Chef built 07-27 partly before the criterion existed, and the results split exactly along it: the **Philly Cheesesteak Stuffed Peppers reheated in the oven and drew the best reheat note on file** ("really good for the reheat, just threw right back in the oven"), while the **Paella's shrimp went "rubbery and tough" in the microwave.** The signal is sharper than "braise good, sear bad" — it is about **the reheat appliance the format implies.** Oven-reheatable formats (stuffed peppers, casseroles, bakes, ziti) are the strongest tier the kitchen has found; microwave-only formats depend entirely on the protein surviving a microwave. **Recommendation to the Chef: for each dish, name the reheat method on the recipe card ("reheat 350°F oven 15 min" / "microwave, covered, 2 min").** Sean will follow it, and it converts a 4★ into a 5★.
- **Substitution-depressed scores are now a measurement problem, not just a shopping problem.** Two of five dishes this week were cooked without a defining ingredient — **lemongrass missing** from the Vietnamese meatballs (Sean: "maybe that's the game changer right there and I missed it") and **chorizo missing** from the Paella. Both scored 4★ instead of a likely 5★. **Recommendation: neither dish should be treated as a weak recipe or moved toward the watch list. Both deserve a clean re-run with the full ingredient list.** And: when a recipe has a single ingredient that carries its identity, the shopping list should say so out loud ("LEMONGRASS — this is the dish; do not substitute").
- 🛒 **MAJOR SOURCING CHANGE — the shopping list has a new reader.** Sean states it directly: he has **"officially moved away from Instacart as the source of truth"** and now **builds a King Soopers pickup cart in the King Soopers app from the actual shopping list**, and is considering dropping Instacart entirely. **The produce-count rule survives and matters more than ever, but its framing as an "Instacart translation" workaround is obsolete.** Write the list for a human standing in the King Soopers app: exact counts, exact package sizes, and a flag on anything a substitution would break. (Standing Preferences still reads "King Soopers via Instacart" — human-editable, left for Sean.)
- **Blank-field handling — a first in eight weeks.** The Philly Cheesesteak's "Cook again?" field came back **empty**. At 5★ with a glowing note the intent is obvious, but the Critic does not infer: it is logged as **Not specified**, and the dish is treated as eligible-to-recycle on its star rating alone. Flagged to the Developer as a dashboard/parser gap.
- **Relative scoring is real and the Chef should know about it.** Sean explicitly graded on a curve this week: "a lot of fire dishes this week, so when comparing to the others, this one was less special." A 4★ in a strong week is not the same signal as a 4★ in a weak one. **Do not treat a single 4★ as a demotion.**
- **New technique worth reusing: the cornstarch crust.** Sean called it out unprompted — "that cornstarch gets such a nice crisp on the surface of the salmon." Dredging fish or protein in cornstarch before the sear is now a proven crowd-pleaser; apply it beyond salmon.
- **Two explicit user requests to honor:** (1) the **Philly cheesesteak filling on a hoagie** at some point — Sean asked by name; (2) **season the bell peppers before the pre-cook** — unseasoned peppers "kind of dulled the Philly cheese steak flavor." Bake both into the recipe card next time that dish is served.
- **Yogurt guidance holds and is now vindicated.** ~1 yogurt-forward sauce per week maximum, and **never as the primary body of a creamy pasta or a spice-forward sauce**. Weeks 07-27 and 08-03 both carry zero. Use heavy cream, coconut milk, tomato, or a pan-butter emulsion instead.
- **Difficulty estimates recovered.** After the 07-20 "harder than described" (whole flank steak to med-rare), week 07-27 came back **5-for-5 "as-expected."** Whatever the Chef changed in how it describes effort is working — keep it, including explicit doneness methods on whole cuts and honest times on multi-component bowls.
- Protein-format signal, not protein signal — **now confirmed five ways**: pork chops missed (3★/No) while ground pork is 4★ twice; Lomo Saltado missed while every other beef format is 5★; Greek meatballs missed on the yogurt/tzatziki format while chicken is otherwise 5★; Cajun shrimp missed on a yogurt cream sauce; and **shrimp itself came back 4★ the moment the sauce changed.** **Judge formats and sauces, not proteins.**
- Mississippi Pot Roast is 5★ twice — a locked-in permanent favorite; the "4 meals of leftovers" value is exactly the reheat-friendly profile Sean needs. Last served 07-13, so it is **back in range for week 08-10.**
- Garlic-butter chicken + broccoli remains 2-for-2 at 5★; adopt Sean's mods (pasta added, broccoli par-boiled) into the recipe card next time it's served.
- Sauce-sopper insight still open: warmed baguette slices stood around the rim of the bowl to soak up sauce — Sean called it a "perfect use case." Reuse on saucy skillet/stew dishes.
- Never-cooked early-reuse pool: **Cajun Honey-Butter Shrimp Bowls (dropped 06-29)** — its two risk nouns have both improved (shrimp exonerated; Cajun's failure isolated to the yogurt sauce, and this dish is honey-butter). **It is now genuinely eligible** — but as a shrimp dish it is best-eaten-fresh, so it should go on a **weekend** slot if used.
- Week 07-27 produced **no new drops**, so nothing was added to the early-reuse pool.

## Recipe Recycling Rules
*The Chef reads these when building the weekly menu.*

- ★★★★★ (5): Recycle every 3–4 weeks
- ★★★★ (4): Recycle every 5–6 weeks
- ★★★ (3): Recycle only if explicitly carried over
- ★★ (2) or below: Do not recycle unless Sean requests it
- "Cook again: No" overrides star rating — do not recycle regardless of score
